solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Devious aunt cheated, it can be verified

indicators.note: something devious is crooked and twisted, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: all thirteen letters taken as the raw material

explanation.surface: A crafty aunt cheated, and the swindle can be proved.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma hides that 'it' belongs to the letters being rearranged rather than to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authenticated has been checked and confirmed as genuine, the same as verified.

clue.text: Concerning a top bishop, parochial epic's sorted out

indicators.note: things sorted out are put into a new order, so the preceding letters get rearranged

blocks.note: fourteen letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A long poem about a parish gets tidied up, apparently on church business.
explanation.definitionFit: Archiepiscopal is the adjective for an archbishop, the senior bishop of a province.

clue.text: Union insolence — it arises in spring

blocks.note: TU is short for trade union
lip is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A union's cheek bubbling up when the season turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a bulb flower that comes up out of the ground in springtime.

clue.text: Severely criticised old firm organised trade around India

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the following word's letters are placed in a new order
around says the rearranged word wraps itself about the next item

blocks.note: ex- means former
Co. is the abbreviation for company
the word to be rearranged
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A former company reorganised its trade around India.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of trade become RATED, which then holds I after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To excoriate is literally to strip skin, and figuratively to censure harshly.

clue.text: Design on box?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pattern printed on a carton or a television set
setter's reading: box is an evergreen hedging shrub, clipped into decorative shapes

explanation.walkthrough: Box suggests a cardboard container, but it is the shrub most often clipped into ornamental shapes in gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of shaping shrubs such as box into designs.

clue.text: Top jazz songstress? A star

blocks.note: a cap is a lid or top
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer; the question mark flags an example

explanation.surface: Asking whether a top jazz singer is a true star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A star' looks like praise for the singer but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capella is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: Kicked and pulled audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the word is to be judged by its spoken sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: pulled by a rope or vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone or something was kicked and dragged along.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe a ball is to strike it with the tip of the foot, a kind of kick.

clue.text: One creates a stink? On the contrary!

definitions.text: One creates a stink? On the contrary!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who kicks up a fuss
setter's reading: reverse it, to something that destroys a smell

explanation.walkthrough: To create a stink is idiomatically to complain loudly; the opposite, taken literally, is an item that removes a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant is a product applied to mask or prevent body odour.

clue.text: People we don't like — this sportsman being nasty, one to be included?

indicators.note: nasty suggests something twisted or out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
included says this item goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: thirteen letters taken as raw material
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grumble about an unpleasant sportsman, the sort of person nobody likes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as people we dislike, but 'we' are humanity: these are people who dislike us all.
explanation.definitionFit: Misanthropists hate humankind in general, so they are people who do not like 'us'.

clue.text: Commander left in charge is a pain

blocks.note: CO is commanding officer
the standard abbreviation
i/c is short for in charge

explanation.surface: The commander left behind in charge is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pain' looks like slang for an annoying person but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is a severe griping pain in the abdomen.

clue.text: Energy old President gets with one sausage

blocks.note: pep is vigour
Juan Perón, former president of Argentina
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A former president regains his energy with a single sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried Italian-style salami, a kind of sausage.

clue.text: I am a friend, embracing one in grand manner

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within your arms, so one item goes inside

blocks.note: I'm contracted, apostrophe dropped
a as in 'twice a day', meaning per
the Roman numeral
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone declares friendship while hugging a chosen one, with great pomp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' as in 'twice a day' means per; the one sits inside 'a friend' taken as a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperially means in the manner of an emperor, hence grandly or majestically.

clue.text: Mark loses heart — an unhealthy condition

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word drops its central letter

blocks.note: a comma is a punctuation mark

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark becomes discouraged, which is bad for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name but is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a medical condition.

clue.text: Agent for one managing museum?

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a curator looks after a museum's collection

explanation.surface: An agent acting on behalf of a museum director.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator is someone appointed to manage another's affairs, a legal agent or proxy.

clue.text: Proper lines outside a school

indicators.note: outside says the preceding pieces sit around the next item

blocks.note: prim means correct and proper
RY is railway, lines of track
taken as written

explanation.surface: Neat lines drawn outside a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A primary is a school for young children, the first stage of education.

clue.text: Island's wild animal, one getting cold on top and bottom

blocks.note: the Roman numeral
C for cold, as on taps
the eland is an African antelope
the same one-and-cold pair repeated at the foot

explanation.surface: A wild beast on an island, one shivering from head to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one getting cold' gives IC, and 'on top and bottom' puts it at both ends of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Icelandic means belonging to Iceland, so it can stand for the island's.

clue.text: Alongside is an animal crossing river

indicators.note: to cross something is to straddle it, so the river sits inside

blocks.note: a beast is an animal
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An animal swimming across a river keeps level with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side, level with one another.

clue.text: English king surrounded by wise men who look for truth maybe?

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the first items inside the next

blocks.note: seers are prophets
the standard abbreviation
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: An English monarch among sages, all searching for truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Seekers are people searching for something, such as spiritual truth; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Tiny holes in floor covering in colonnade

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a stoa is a Greek covered colonnade
a mat covers part of a floor

explanation.surface: Little holes worn in a rug in a classical walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomata are the microscopic pores in a leaf through which gases pass.

clue.text: Wife dumped by author outside church — I understood the quaking!

indicators.note: to be dumped is to be dropped, so that letter is taken away
outside says the shortened word goes round the next item

blocks.note: an author is a writer
the standard abbreviation
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A jilted wife's author waits outside church, and someone feels the tremor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: the Richter scale makes sense of an earthquake's strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Richter devised the scale for measuring earthquakes, so his name is what grasps quaking.

clue.text: Most offensive row is "not English"

blocks.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A furious argument about whether something is English.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel but is a line; 'is' in another language is the French est.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling or grossly offensive, so rankest is the superlative.

clue.text: Test hard material lacking carbon

indicators.note: lacking means without, so one letter is removed

blocks.note: coral is a hard reef-forming substance
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Testing a hard substance for carbon content.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Features of a square dance in trading establishment

blocks.note: a square has four corners
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A square dance held in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square dance' looks like one phrase but splits across two pieces; a corner shop is a small local grocery store in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner shop is a small neighbourhood store selling everyday goods.

clue.text: Army hospital with tidiness falling short

indicators.note: falling short means not reaching the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
order is neatness

explanation.surface: A military hospital that is not quite tidy enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or host, and an army in older usage.

clue.text: Your turn in Paris to upset foreign character

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

blocks.note: à toi is French for your turn

explanation.surface: A game in Paris where it's your turn to unsettle a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Recording medium — a duo worked with it to get copy

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: letters taken as written
taken as written
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: A pair of musicians work at a track to produce a copy on cassette.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiotape is magnetic tape for recording sound.

clue.text: Specifications for limited periods

blocks.note: first meaning: conditions of an agreement
second meaning: fixed spans of time, such as school or office tenures

explanation.definitionFit: Terms are both the stipulated conditions of a contract and fixed spans of time such as school terms.

clue.text: After end of play stage will be left so dull?

blocks.clueFragment: After end of play stage will be left so dull?
blocks.note: surface reading: once a show closes the theatre is lifeless
setter's reading: when the play finishes the stage has no cast members on it

explanation.walkthrough: The roles in a play are its characters; when they have all gone, the stage is literally without them, which is also the word for bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking character means lacking distinctive qualities, hence dull and featureless.
